groups.title: Check a resolver change before it merges, and see what is still unsettled
groups.blurb: Both consumers decide tonnages from this package, so every change runs the parity report before it merges -- it reads each consumer's resolver out of its git object store at a pinned ref, never a working tree, and exit 1 is a disagreement or a comparison it could not establish (neither is a pass). It needs ../fsg-tender-review and ../fsg-bluebeam-steel-standards checked out. The known-issues run reports and never gates: it prints OBSERVED beside EXPECTED so the open estimator questions cannot quietly outlive their subject.

groups.title: Regenerate the packaged section library from the estimating workbook
groups.blurb: The section library and labour rates are a generated snapshot of the workbook's 90_Lists -- never hand-edit data/fsg_sections.json; change the workbook and re-run this. --check re-reads the workbook and compares the content hash, which is the only thing that answers whether the copy still matches; an age threshold cannot. Read-only against the workbook, and a merge here changes nothing downstream until each consumer moves its pin.

groups.title: Find a command, and keep this repo's own index honest
groups.blurb: `docs/COMMANDS.md` is generated from the tracked tree, so it cannot quietly fall behind the code. `--check` exits 1 when it has, or when a new command has no task group yet.

groups.title: Prep for the GitHub-org rename (crm#655 gate line 7)
groups.blurb: The five repos are moving from `Rostov-au` to an FSG-owned org. `rename_github_org.py` catalogues (default) or, with `--apply`, rewrites every literal `Rostov-au/` across all five repos' tracked files -- dry run by default, the new org name is never guessed, and it never commits or pushes. Prep only as of tr#669 (15 Sep 2026): the org does not exist yet, so `--apply` has only ever been run against a throwaway clone.

groups.title: Check a pull request body before it merges
groups.blurb: David's rule, all five repos, 16 Sep 2026: no commit carries a co-authorship trailer and no pull request or document carries an AI-tool attribution banner line. `check_pr_body.py` refuses a PR body or first comment that carries either, case-insensitively; run it locally with `--body-file`, or let `pr-body.yml` run it on every open/edit/push. `fsg-estimating-crm` carries the same script with two extra rules (a closing keyword, a word limit) this repo has never adopted.

groups.title: Check the estate-wide compulsory reading path stays under its word cap
groups.blurb: crm#557/crm#635, estate-wide rollout 19 Sep 2026: one CLAUDE.md per repo must stay under 7,500 words in total, because a doc edit in any one repo can push the shared total over and turn an unrelated repo's PRs red. Narrowed, not raised, 25 Sep 2026 (crm#1009): fsg-tender-review/docs/README.md is no longer counted -- it is read on demand, not at session start, and removing it from the count restored real headroom without trimming any content. The real logic lives in `fsg_common.reading_path` -- this is fsg-common's own thin wrapper, same as the copy in each of the other four repos; each names which repo it is running in and calls the shared `main()`. Needs FSG_COMMON_PAT (or GH_TOKEN/GITHUB_TOKEN) to read the four private repos over the API; refuses rather than passing without one.

groups.title: Open a pull request, and merge one only when it is green
groups.blurb: crm#1719: the PR helpers every repo shares, wrapped from `fsg_common.gh_pr_create` and `fsg_common.merge_on_green`. `gh_pr_create.py` strips attribution lines and runs the PR-body check BEFORE the PR exists, so the gate cannot fail after the fact; `merge_on_green.py` refuses a red, draft, conflicting or badly-bodied PR, waits for pending checks, squash-merges and prunes the local worktree. A check that never ran is absent, not passed.
